bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled archive entry name was appended to a temporary extraction-directory path and opened for output without canonical normalization or a containment check. A traversal entry could therefore escape the staging directory, overwrite a server-writable file, and then have that escaped file deleted by cleanup. The advisory PoC exercises ZIP through ZipUtils.unpackFile; the same unchecked construction also existed in the sibling RAR path and was reachable from configured EmailReceiver unpacking and MakeUnzipFileAction.
flaw_origin: Commit 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 first created an affected lifecycle by adding opt-in archive unpacking to EmailReceiver and writing ZIP and RAR entry names directly beneath an output-directory string. Commit ce3cf594f118e720279abdb78116a597956bbe41 later added the same unsafe mechanism to MakeUnzipFileAction. Commit 4950d66839375b11a4706fe1b5bd5f28ec9abf17 merely centralized the existing implementations in ZipUtils and routed both callers to it, so that move/refactor is not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827` shows human author and committer Vandrouny <filipchyk.andrei@gmail.com>, one parent, and only the subject `[server] Опция распаковки архивов при приёме почты`; it contains no AI/bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The assigned fix_sha disagreement was primary 547f9c92df24969fb34f6d7009bfeb3d7727c67a versus reviewer 90d058b9007c1e9b0babc0aac50fe2f292fb947d. The reviewer wins. `git show 1aefa1fd67bb644e6d4f5682051fc85b81048322 -- ZipUtils.java` shows the March source patch only wrapping ZIP file entries in `!filePath.contains("../")`; `git show 547f9c92df24969fb34f6d7009bfeb3d7727c67a` records that it is a cherry-pick of 1aefa1fd67bb644e6d4f5682051fc85b81048322, and stable patch-id gives the same 4ba1c5411569c90ccac57099811a1285acbe05db for both. That partial check does not cover backslash traversal on Windows, ZIP directory entries, or the manual RAR output path. `git show 90d058b9007c1e9b0babc0aac50fe2f292fb947d -- ZipUtils.java` replaces the string test with canonical-path `isInsideDirectory` checks on ZIP files, ZIP directories, and RAR entries. `git log --all --reverse -S'isInsideDirectory' -- ZipUtils.java` returns only 90d058b9007c1e9b0babc0aac50fe2f292fb947d; its direct parent bc091770fd0f86050a0056b375d40728166fb423 still has only `contains("../")`. Although 90d058b9 also updates junrar, it is a one-parent directly authored commit, not an import, merge, move, or squash aggregate, and it is the smallest repository commit that introduces the complete containment fix. For the version boundary, `git merge-base --is-ancestor 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 6.1` succeeds; 547f9c92 is absent from 6.1 and present in 6.2, while 90d058b9 is not an ancestor of 6.2 and `git tag --contains 90d058b9` returns no tag. Revision grep shows 6.1 has no guard, 6.2 has only `contains("../")`, and master has canonical checks for all three paths. Thus 6.2 is only partially remediated and no tagged release in this clone contains the complete source fix. The first-party issue #1545 names ZipUtils.unpackFile, EmailReceiver, and MakeUnzipFileAction, supplies a ZIP PoC, and states affected through 6.1; the bundle GHSA metadata says `<= 6.0-beta2` and supplies no first patched version. For the BIC boundary, `git show 557102b6 -- EmailReceiver.java` adds the opt-in unpack dispatcher and both unchecked extractors, while `git grep -E 'unpackZIPFile|unpackRARFile|unpack\[Account\]' 6747b4ead5e8f26ccd36ecb33e77aa9ea9335fe1` returns no match. BIC-only `git cat-file -p` supplies no AI signal.
reasoning: The earliest real vulnerable change is the 2017 EmailReceiver unpack feature: its immediate parent lacks the activation property and both extraction sinks. The later MakeUnzipFileAction copy and ZipUtils centralization are not smaller origins. On the disputed fix, the primary treated the March release cherry-pick as final because it crossed the 6.2 tag boundary, but direct diff inspection proves that patch is only a forward-slash ZIP-file-entry filter and leaves the same containment mechanism reachable through other entry forms. The July one-parent commit is the first history object that applies canonical containment to every affected extraction branch, so it is both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha even though no release tag contains it. The BIC commit object is human-authored and has no AI marker; the Claude co-author trailer on the much later fix is outside the protocol's BIC-only attribution rule. The gate-complete verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
